create.name: Confluence Zen Center STL
create.bio:
Confluence Zen Center STL is a small Soto Zen sangha that sits in a house at the edge of Maplewood, in the St. Louis area of Missouri. Its teacher, Rev. Daigaku Rummé, was born in Iowa in 1950 and ordained in 1978 by Sekkei Harada Roshi, under whom he trained for over twenty-seven years at Hosshin-ji, a monastery in Fukui, Japan. He later worked for the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center in San Francisco and directed its North America office while serving as head priest of Zenshuji in Los Angeles, before settling in St. Louis in 2015. He has translated books by Harada Roshi and, more recently, Inoue Gien Roshi's commentary on Keizan's Denkoroku.

Zazen is held early on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday mornings and on Monday evenings, each closing with a short sutra service. Sundays follow a monthly rotation of sitting, walking meditation and service, with a Dharma talk and tea on one Sunday and shared work on another, and most months include a full one-day sitting with an oryoki meal and dokusan. Newcomers are pointed to a monthly Beginner's Night on a Tuesday evening, which teaches zendo forms and how to sit before a period of zazen and time for questions.

courses.title: Beginner's Night
courses.description: A monthly evening, usually the first Tuesday, for people new to Zen or to the centre: an introduction to zendo etiquette and sitting posture, two short periods of zazen with walking meditation, a chant and time for questions. Check the calendar for the date.

courses.title: One-Day Sitting
courses.description: A monthly full day of zazen and kinhin from 8 am, with sutra services, a Dharma talk, lunch, work practice and dokusan with the teacher in the afternoon. Participants need not stay for the whole schedule.

courses.title: Sunday Practice
courses.description: Sunday mornings of two zazen periods with walking meditation and a service, rotating through the month between a Dharma talk with tea, work practice and the one-day sitting.

free_resources.title: Weekday Zazen
free_resources.description: Morning zazen on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday and an evening sitting on Monday, each followed by a short sutra service, with the chant for each day listed.
